VERDICT: CLEAN

Second review (Opus, read-only). This PR was already merged; the build check is post-merge run 44596948231.

## What I checked

**Explain off gives byte-identical output.** Each script calls `explain(a)` and adds the text only when it is non-empty. The helper returns "" when the option is off. The `pin()` test asserts the absent and the off programs are equal. The strip-and-compare check rebuilds the off program from the on program, line by line. I also diffed head `f1485e26e` against the merge commit `e048b103c` for every file this PR touched. There is no difference; the merge added no hand edits.

**Comment forms.** `sinumerik.cps` declares `explains = "semi"`; the helper emits `; text` to the block end. The other seven declare `"paren"`. The helper strips `()%;` from the text, and leads a comment that opens with an executable keyword (MSG, DEBUG, PY, …) with "- ". A comment-only line gets no append: `explain()` stops at a token that starts with "(" or ";". I found no path that adds an explanation to a line that already ends with a comment word.

**The 80-character cap.** All eight guards read `if (c && line.length + 1 + c.length <= 80) line += " " + c;`. These scripts write printable ASCII, so `.length` is the byte count. TinyG still checks its own 191-byte limit before the append, so the comment can never push a line over it. A guard can only omit a comment; it never shortens an executable word.

**Machine EDM codes.** In `wire-iso.cps`, every `block()` call that writes a `code()` value passes `machineCode = true` (lines 275, 280, 281, 298, 299, 346, 347, 350, 362, 365, 401, 404, 405). The other calls write ISO words only. The adversarial test sets the codes to T91, T90, M3, M4 and G99 and pins that each line stays unexplained. In `sinker-iso.cps` the machine codes go through `emit()`, which never explains. The mixed tapered move at line 365 loses its G1 explanation; that is conservative and safe.

**Word meanings.** Sinumerik G700/G710 are the inch and millimetre programming words; that is correct for 840D. G505/G506 as WORK OFFSET 5/6 match this post's own mapping (G54..G57, G505, G506, #934). G58/G59 map to "" so the mill reading cannot appear; the test pins it. The plasma meanings match the published Tormach 1300PL manual (sections 7.1-7.2): M200 AutoFS, M205 torch off, M207/M208/M209 with P. The lathe G59.1/G59.2/G59.3 as WORK OFFSET 7/8/9 are correct for the LinuxCNC extended offsets.

**Tests.** Each dialect has a golden compare, a warnings check and a swallowed-records check. `block_budget` proves short lines get the comment and long lines stay unchanged.

## Nits, not blockers (comment text only; the program is unaffected)

- `tormach-plasma.cps`: G16 says "TORCH ON". The manual names G16 "Pierce" and names M203 "Start Torch". "PIERCE" would be the better wording.
- `tormach-plasma.cps`: G15 says "PROBE PLATE". The manual names it "Workpiece Probe" (ohmic). Consider "PROBE WORKPIECE".

Heidenhain and Sodick keep their named refusals; the tests pin them. Provenance of the added texts is the two public Tormach manuals and the Siemens 840D documentation, in the decision file.
